American Board of Pediatrics (ABP): General Pediatrics Certifying Examination (conditional ABP–ABPN pediatrics-neurology pathway after qualifying supervised training)
boardStatus: ABPN publishes a distinct initial Child Neurology certification examination. Its December 15, 2025 content specifications describe one 400-question exam titled Certification Examination in Neurology with Special Qualification in Child Neurology (60% child neurology, 40% adult neurology). ABP separately offers a conditional General Pediatrics certification examination pathway for candidates completing specified accredited pediatrics and child-neurology training. Neurodevelopmental Disabilities is a different pathway/field, not a synonym. A generic directory category does not create a separate board.
boardEligibilityNotice: This independent self-study curriculum does not confer exam eligibility. Check current ABPN and ABP requirements and obtain official verification of accredited training. No pass guarantee.

boardEligibilityNotice: Do not infer board eligibility from programme name, NRMP code, or this curriculum. ABPN pages reviewed 2026-10-07 say usual CAP candidates must be ABPN-certified in Psychiatry by the deadline specified for the CAP exam, complete two full years/24 calendar months of CAP training, and satisfy other current requirements; Psychiatry primary certification has its own PGY-1 plus post-PGY-1 training, outpatient continuity and clinical skills requirements. Confirm a specific trainee’s route, current ACGME programme status, accepted PGY-1, training credit and exact eligibility with ABPN and programme leadership. Current public evidence does not establish MGH/McLean’s ACGME accreditation status as a combined programme. No eligibility is promised.

boardStatus: ABTS is the primary certifying board for thoracic surgery, including cardiac and general thoracic domains. Primary certification uses Part I written and Part II oral examinations. boardEligibilityNotice: ABTS determines board eligibility after its pathway, application, license and other requirements. This course does not make a learner board-eligible, confer ABS/ABTS certification, replace medical school/residency, or authorize practice. ABTS notes ABS certification is optional for certain thoracic residents beginning after July 2003; no general-surgery eligibility is implied. ACGME’s approved 4+3 pathway can lead to eligibility for general and thoracic certification subject to approvals and all board criteria.
